figures.caption: Fig. 3. Schematic illustrations and cross-sectional optical microscopy images of all measurement setups. A) Type-A cells: Symmetrical cells with the layers: composite electrode|electrolyte|composite electrode were employed for TLM-based measurements; B) Type-B cells: Symmetrical cells with the layers: lithium metal |electro- lyte|composite electrode|electrolyte|lithium metal were used to measure the Li+ current through the composite electrode under electron-blocking conditions; C) Type-C cells: Symmetrical cells with the layers: lithium metal | electrolyte | composite electrode| electrolyte | composite electrode | electrolyte | lithium metal were employed to carry out both types of measurements on the same composite electrodes.

figures.caption: Fig. 4. Impedance spectra obtained for symmetrical type-A cells shown in Fig. 3A, with diﬀerent thickness of both composite electrode layers, dcomposites. In order to facilitate the comparison of the spectra, the electrolyte resistance Relectrolyte was subtracted. Interfacial resistances between the layers were not detectable. The solid lines represent the best ﬁts to Eq. (5). The total ionic conductivity of the pure electrolyte was σion,electrolyte,25 °C = 0.68 mS cm−1.

figures.caption: Fig. 6. Impedance spectrum for a type-B cell shown in Fig. 3B. The spectrum was recorded in a frequency range from 0.5 MHz to 70 mHz on a sample with a volume fraction of the solid electrolyte of ε = 0.66. The average thickness of the composite-electrode was 393 μm, and the ionic conductivity of the pure elec- trolyte was σion,electrolyte,25 °C = 0.81 mS cm−1. The solid line represents the best ﬁt to Eq. (12).

figures.caption: Fig. 7. Comparison of a TLM-based impedance measurement (black squares) and a Li+ current measurements under electron-blocking conditions (blue cir- cles) for a sample with a volume fraction of the solid electrolyte of ε = 0.66. The LPSI electrolyte resistance was subtracted from both spectra. The solid lines represent the best ﬁts to Eq. (5) and to Eq. (12), respectively. The thickness of both composite electrodes was 780 μm, and the ionic conductivity of the pure electrolyte was σion,electrolyte,25 °C = 0.78 mS cm−1. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this ﬁgure legend, the reader is referred to the Web version of this article.)

figures.caption: Fig. 8. A) Relation between eﬀective tortuosity τeff and volume fraction of the solid electrolyte, ε , obtained from the TLM-based measurements (black squares) and from the Li+ current measurements under electron-blocking condition (blue circles). The Bruggeman exponent α was determined from the linear ﬁt in the log-log plot in a volume fraction range = ε 0.4 – 0.66. B) Eﬀective ionic conductivity of the composite electrode calculated from the Li+ current measurements under electron- blocking condition as illustrated in Fig. 3B. The blue dots represent the data measured in this study.
